Senior Software Engineer & Consultant, Boise, Idaho

C#/.NET, Microsoft Power Platform, and AI integration, with Python, C++, and JavaScript when the job calls for it. Founder of Beyond the Vale LLC.

Cody Peterson

I’m a software engineer in Boise and I run a small consulting company called Beyond the Vale. I started as a DevOps Engineer, moved into a Tech Lead role, and now work as an Architect on a large-scale government platform, designing backend services in C#/.NET, building on Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, mentoring developers, and making sure the systems I build actually hold up under real-world pressure.

I like all kinds of programming. C# is home, but I write Python, C++, and JavaScript, and the projects I enjoy most tend to be the odd ones: a computer-vision turret, a VR physics sandbox, a multiplayer game with WebSocket state sync, a console app that saves somebody a week. Whether it’s a CI/CD pipeline that cuts deploys from 4 hours to 15 minutes or a Power Automate flow that retires a spreadsheet, I care about building things that work well and are built to last.

Languages: C# (primary) · Python · C++ · JavaScript / TypeScript · PowerShell · SQL

Working Together

I communicate directly and keep the technical noise low. You get clear status updates, honest assessments when something isn’t viable, and architecture decisions explained in terms of trade-offs, not jargon. I don’t disappear once scoping is done.

Most work is scoped as a fixed-price project so there’s nothing open-ended for you to approve; bigger builds run on a retainer. For agencies and dev shops, I work white-label under your name on your paper. And I’ve spent years inside Azure Government with its compliance requirements and approval chains, so real constraints don’t slow me down much.

My preference is to own problems end-to-end: from discovery and architecture through implementation and production. I’ll tell you what I think the right approach is, explain why, and build it. If your requirements change mid-project, we adapt. The goal is a system that works reliably, not one that looks good in a slide deck.

AI-Augmented Development

I use AI tooling (Claude API, Claude Code) daily as a force multiplier, not as a crutch but as an accelerant for the parts of engineering that benefit from it. More importantly, I’ve built production AI integrations: multi-provider LLM abstraction layers, rate limiting, caching, fallback chains, and RAG patterns. I work in this space as an architect, not just a user.
